A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Regression Trees Know Calculus, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C. Complete text comparison and visual inspection support reliable judgments despite appendix reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original regression benchmarks, synthetic active-subspace experiments, NHEFS and MNIST analyses in Section 5, and classification experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Table 1, Figures 2–7, and the additional analysis in Appendix B.3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1's tree-gradient extraction procedure and the active-subspace and integrated-gradient estimators in Sections 3–4 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight regression benchmarks, low- and high-dimensional synthetic tasks, NHEFS data, MNIST digit comparisons, and median-threshold classification variants in Appendix C.

E2.justification: Id, PCA, and Rand remain the rotation comparators. GP, PRA, and DASM remain the low-dimensional active-subspace comparators, with DASM retained for the high-dimensional comparison. Appendix C also retains its comparator set.

E3.justification: Tree and forest depths, 100-fold cross-validation, synthetic dimensions and sample-size ranges, NHEFS fitting settings, and the 500-point integrated-gradient procedure are unchanged. Appendix relocation introduces no protocol revision.

E4.justification: The sparse-subspace investigation, NHEFS and MNIST case analyses, and supplementary classification study remain unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or additional analysis is introduced or removed.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains its confidence-interval-overlap bolding, Figure 6 retains the cross-validation boxplots, and Appendix B.2 still reports 20 repetitions. No statistical reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: Table 1 values, the graphical results in Figures 2–7, and Appendix B.3's eigenvector entries are unchanged. The reported rankings, trends, and qualitative findings also match after accounting for appendix relocation.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations, Proposition 1, Corollaries 1–3, and their Appendix A proofs are unchanged. Different page breaks do not alter the mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and Section 6 retain the same claims about extracting gradients from trees, enabling gradient-based interpretation, and estimating active subspaces efficiently.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are retained, including dependence on the chosen neural baseline configuration, difficulties with dense high-dimensional gradients, and the less promising classification findings in Appendix C.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same dataset access information, software packages, network width and learning rate, hardware, and runtime disclosures. The spelling correction to 'implemented' adds no technical information.

R1.justification: v2 removes the bibliography entry for Louppe et al. (2013), Understanding variable importances in forests of randomized trees, which was not cited in the body. The related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 updates the author's affiliation and contact information and makes a handful of spelling corrections, including 'projectin' to 'projection' and 'physic-informed' to 'physics-informed'. The narrative and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Appendix layout changes: Appendix A begins after the references on page 11, Figure 6 is centered on a page by itself, and Appendix C's discussion appears together below Figure 7. Figure content, captions, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The spelling corrections and removal of an uncited bibliography entry provide only slight editorial polish. Methods, proofs, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged, while appendix reflow produces no meaningful overall quality difference.
